idiom_name: URI objects as href + Hash link elements + Net::HTTP dereference
implementation_notes: Ruby's uri standard library supplies the link address as a first-class RFC 3986 object: URI.join(base, segment) or URI::HTTP.build mints the href, and the object answers scheme, host, path, query, and request_uri, so a link element is just a Hash of relation metadata ({'rel' =>, 'href' => URI, 'method' =>, 'type' =>}) riding in the response body or message payload. The consumer selects the link by rel, coerces the href back with URI() if it traveled as a String, and dereferences it with Net::HTTP.get(URI(link['href'])) or a Net::HTTP.start session - Net::HTTP is designed to work directly with URI objects and turns on TLS verification for https hrefs automatically. JSON.generate / JSON.parse carry the link across process boundaries (URI objects serialize via to_s inside the hash). The classic structure collapses into uri + net/http + hashes; a full link-object class hierarchy is only justified when building a reusable HATEOAS client SDK (as hypermedia client wrappers in the Rails/Faraday ecosystem do).
code_sketch:
require 'uri'; require 'net/http'; require 'json'

# Producer: mint links and embed them in the response carrier
base = 'https://api.example.com/orders/42'
_links = [
  {'rel' => 'self',    'href' => URI.join(base).freeze,                'method' => 'GET'},
  {'rel' => 'payment', 'href' => URI.join(base, 'payment').freeze,      'method' => 'GET',
   'type' => 'application/json'}
]
payload = JSON.generate('order' => {'id' => 42}, '_links' => _links)

# Consumer: navigate by relation, never by constructed URL
link = JSON.parse(payload)['_links'].find { |l| l['rel'] == 'payment' }
raise 'payment is read-only' unless link['method'] == 'GET'
body = Net::HTTP.get(URI(link['href']))
pitfalls: URI objects are mutable (path=, query=): a shared link whose href gets rewritten after handoff silently repoints every holder - freeze the URI (and the metadata Hash) so links stay immutable values.

Stringly-typed links: storing href as a raw String defers validation to dereference time; parse with URI() at production (it raises URI::InvalidURIError immediately) instead of shipping a link that fails only when followed.

Acting on a link without checking its method/type contract: in Ruby's duck-typed ecosystem nothing stops code from POSTing to a rel that only granted a GET - enforce the method check before dereferencing.

Following links recursively without a visited set or depth budget: a cycle among _links entries becomes runaway Net::HTTP requests until the stack or the network gives out - track visited hrefs and cap depth.

Default Net::HTTP timeouts are generous (60 s open/read) and every Net::HTTP.start holds a socket, so unbounded link fan-out piles up threads and descriptors - set open_timeout/read_timeout explicitly and reuse sessions for multi-link traversal.

URI.join against an internal request base leaks hostnames and ports (http://10.0.0.3:8080/...) to external consumers - emit relative or registry-backed hrefs and treat href as an address, never as an authorization grant.
